answer: Because the shale fee is applied at the lotus exit, the harbor audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 11% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
